title: Adapted Boxing and Photography in Haematology: Body Image and Self-Esteem
official: A Study to Assess the Impact of Adapted Boxing and Photography on Body Image and Self-esteem Among Haematology Inpatients
summary: Although the benefits of adapted physical activity (APA) are well documented in the scientific literature, few studies have specifically examined the impact of adapted boxing on body image and self-esteem in patients with haematological conditions. The current approach relies on the empirical observations of healthcare professionals, but no systematic evaluation has been conducted to quantify the actual effects of this practice on patients. This project therefore aims to address this lack of data by rigorously and scientifically assessing the impact of a boxing session on patients' psychological and emotional well-being. The use of validated questionnaires (Rosenberg Scale, QIC, EORTC QLQ-C30) will provide objective and comparable measures12.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Patients aged 18 or over
2. Patients diagnosed with cancer currently undergoing treatment in a haematology department (e.g. leukaemia, lymphoma, multiple myeloma, etc.), at various stages of their treatment journey
3. Patients considered sufficiently stable to undertake adapted physical activity following medical assessment (no medical contraindications to practising adapted boxing) and for whom it is offered as part of their standard care
4. Patients who have given their consent to participate in the study
5. Patients covered by a statutory health insurance scheme
6. Patients who have been prescribed adapted physical activity by a doctor

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Minors
2. Individuals subject to a court-ordered protective measure (judicial protection order, guardianship, curatorship, etc.)
3. Inability to provide the individual with informed consent (difficulties in understanding, insufficient command of French, etc.)
4. Patients with neurological or psychiatric disorders, including severe depression
5. Pregnant women (this criterion will be recorded based on the patient's statement)
6. Breastfeeding women
